correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructs \(f_q(d)\) from binomial counts and \(\Delta_d=d(1-q)^2q^{d-1}\); ratio \(q(d+1)/d\) gives strict discrete concavity at low q and strict convexity at high q. Exchange arguments prove and distinguish maximizing degree multisets; a cyclic primary-label construction proves all feasible multisets are graph-realizable without isolates. In the intermediate range, two exact improving transfers prove the one-middle-degree and balanced-high-degree necessary conditions, making \(O(nm^2)\) candidate enumeration exhaustive. Uniform sampling of a random extinction ordering and cut gives \((d-1)/(d+1)\), strictly concave in integer degree. The actual packaged verifier enumerates primary-state probabilities and 3,605 degree-optimization instances with exact fractions. Universal claims rest on the algebraic proof, not finite numerical scans.

originality.rationale: Existing ecological robustness literature establishes random-removal network robustness, degree balancing under an all-partners-lost rule, stochastic partial-loss extinctions, and general threshold survival formulas. It does not state or imply the exact sharp two-surviving-partner balanced/concentrated phase boundaries, the intermediate optimizer structure, or the contrasting two-survivor all-stage optimum. Semantic and exact searches found no same claim; a possible abstract resource-allocation reduction and supplements are residual risks.
residual_risks: General discrete single-inflection resource-allocation theory may give a stronger abstract structural result under unrelated terminology; mathematical exchange principles themselves are not new.
Supplementary appendices of threshold-ecology papers have not all been inspected in complete form, even though the most plausible primary article body and the closest optimizing section were read.
Empirical partner thresholds and actual extinction events may violate the fixed two-survivor deterministic criterion and independent equal-probability primary losses.

value.rationale: Fixed-edge ecological network robustness is an established conservation-network target. Requiring two partners instead of just one creates genuine redundancy-dependent response. The theorem gives sharp parameter boundaries distinguishing balanced from concentrated connectivity, an exact structural reduction in the transition regime, and a contrast with full-removal-trajectory robustness that prevents interpreting two distinct objective summaries as interchangeable. These are motivated structural facts rather than arbitrary small-instance computations.
